core.metanarrative_position: Cycle 1 capstone integrates biblical interpretation with worship, character, relationships, service, and ongoing independent growth.

claims.statement: Creation, promise, new-covenant hope, Messiah, church, and new creation are connected movements in the canonical story.
Luke 24 explicitly connects the Scriptures with the Messiah’s suffering, resurrection, and proclamation to the nations.
The project’s Know / Understand / Practise / Become framework is a pedagogical synthesis intended to connect learning with formation; it is not itself an inspired biblical formula.
claims.interpretive_hinge: This is a curriculum-framework conclusion: it follows from the canonical matrix design and the project rule that approved biblical content remains governed by Scripture and review, rather than from a verse explicitly commanding this scheduling structure.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this curriculum-design conclusion as though Scripture directly commands this particular lesson architecture or calendar slot.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that learning is integrated with worship, character, relationships, service, and continued growth.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The principal passage or required editor selection is Genesis 1:26-31.
Learning is integrated with worship, character, relationships, service, and continued growth.
The lesson belongs within the wider Cycle 1 structure.
understand: Meaning depends on immediate context, genre, and the evidence actually available.
Direct textual observation should remain distinguishable from synthesis, inference, framework design, prudential judgment, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before giving an interpretation.
Write a short Cycle 1 reflection naming one conviction strengthened by evidence, one practice to continue, and one question still worth studying.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage or synthesis.
Student can support the big idea with the appropriate evidence class.
Student can distinguish at least one observation from one interpretation, framework choice, prudential decision, or application.

interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Keep genre, audience, historical setting, and literary context visible.

Make room for unresolved questions and identify what evidence would be needed to investigate them.

activities.title: Cycle 1 Capstone Evidence Map
steps: Read the selected evidence and record direct observations.
Place observations, interpretations, framework choices, or prudential applications into the resource categories.
Discuss which conclusions require more than direct textual wording.
Write one careful response that follows from the evidence.
activities.learning_link: Makes the lesson’s evidence classification and formation aim visible.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw the categories on blank paper or complete the exercise verbally.

activities.title: Evidence Class Check
steps: Read several statements connected to the lesson.
Classify each as text observation, synthesis, framework choice, prudential judgment, or application.
Return to the evidence and justify each classification.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Use verbal responses instead of written cards.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what the selected passage reveals and ask for wisdom to respond faithfully.

accessibility.reading_level: Teen independent or guided close reading
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before using theological or curriculum shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read the passage aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe where helpful.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, giving amounts, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, giving, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the selected evidence, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
